parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The repository's name within its owner.

403.description: needs manage_users

get.summary: Needs `read`; the audit log is also checked for callers with `view_audit`.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: The namespace that owns the repository.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The repository's name within its owner.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: check only this path; the audit log is then not checked

404.description: path_not_found for a path without revisions

200.description: sets the HttpOnly session cookie

403.description: right password, but the account cannot sign in: email_not_verified, approval_pending or account_disabled

429.description: too_many_attempts; Retry-After says how many seconds to wait

403.description: csrf_failed

400.description: invalid_request or reserved_name

403.description: invalid_setup_token

429.description: too_many_attempts; Retry-After says how many seconds to wait

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: another user's tokens; needs manage_users in a repository that user belongs to

403.description: asked for a permission the caller lacks in a listed repository

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the token's id

Account.description: The signed-in account, independent of any repository.

admin.description: Runs the server: may approve and disable accounts under `/v1/admin`.

AccountInfo.description: An account as an administrator sees it.

ActivityEntry.description: A file or lock event from the audit log.

action.description: checkout, release, checkin, restore or force_unlock.

key.description: The public key as an OpenSSH line.

title.description: A name for the key; defaults to the key's own comment.

AdminCreateOrgRequest.description: A server administrator or service credential creating an organization for an existing user.

owner.description: An existing active user, who becomes the organization's first owner.

AssembleObjectRequest.description: Chunks already uploaded as objects, to be joined into one object.

chunks.description: SHA-256 hex digests of stored chunks, in order; each at most 4 MiB.

hash.description: SHA-256 hex over the event's canonical encoding, which includes `previous`.

previous.description: The hash of the preceding event in the same log; absent for the first.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to fetch the next, older page; null on the last page.

Branch.description: A branch: a name pointing at a commit. The default branch's `.pyn/pyn.toml` is the repository's policy.

commit.description: The commit the branch points at; null only for the default branch of a repository with no commits.

current.description: Required when the account already has a password.

ChangesetDeletion.description: One path a changeset removes. The path stays in history as a deletion revision (`Revision.deleted`).

base_revision.description: The path's revision on the branch: the one being removed.

ChangesetRequest.description:
Paths checked in and removed together: every base and lock check passes or nothing is written. An exclusive path,
written or removed, needs the caller's live lock, which the commit consumes.

branch.description: The branch the commit is made on; the default branch if omitted.

deletions.description: Paths to remove; a changeset needs at least one entry or deletion.

revisions.description: One revision per requested path: the entries in request order, then the deletions.

base_revision.description: A shared path's revision on the branch, or an exclusive path's newest revision on any branch.

branch.description: The branch the commit is made on; the default branch if omitted.

base_revision.description: Revision the caller's copy is at (omit if none); must equal the head.

branch.description:
The branch the lock is for: the path must be exclusive under that branch's effective policy. The default
branch if omitted.

Commit.description:
One atomic write: a single checkin or a whole changeset, recorded as a git commit on a branch. `id` is the git
commit id, so a commit can be fetched with a unique abbreviation of at least 4 digits.

authored_at.description: The author time, in whole seconds; its timezone is `author.offset_minutes`. Absent from servers that predate it.

changeset.description: Set when the commit was made as a changeset.

created_at.description: The committer time, in whole seconds.

message.description: The message decoded lossily; a commit's exact bytes are never altered.

parents.description: Empty for the first commit of the repository, otherwise the commit it was made on top of.

revisions.description: The revisions the commit made, ordered by path.

signature.description: The commit's `gpgsig` header, when it is signed.

tree.description: The id of the root git tree of the repository as of this commit.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to fetch the next, older page; null on the last page.

name.description: Git ref rules apply: no spaces, none of `~ ^ : ? * [ \`, no `..`.

start.description: A branch name, or a commit id or abbreviation of at least 4 digits; the default branch's head if omitted.

hours.description: How long the invitation can be used, in hours.

name.description: Shares the namespace with user names: 2 to 39 lowercase letters, digits, `-` or `_`, not reserved.

max_locks_per_user.description: Locks one user may hold; defaults to the server's. A limit in the repository's policy file overrides it.

owner.description:
The namespace to create it in: the caller's own account name, or an organization whose repository-creation
policy lets them. Defaults to the caller.

name.description: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, `-` or `_`; unique, and never reused after revocation.

description.description: At most 500 characters; defaults to empty.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters; defaults to the slug.

slug.description: 1 to 39 lowercase letters, digits, `-` or `_`, starting with a letter or digit; unique in the organization.

repos.description: Repositories the token is valid for, as `owner/name`; at least one.

code.description: Give this to the person being invited. Shown once and never stored.

secret.description: Presented as a bearer credential. Shown once and never stored.

token.description: The token to present as a bearer credential. Shown once and never stored.

CreationEffect.description: Whether a creation rule permits or forbids.

CreationRuleInfo.description: A subject holds at most one rule per effect. A matching `deny` beats any `allow`.

subject.description: The team slug, user name, or organization role (`owner` or `member`).

CreationScope.description: Which repository visibilities a rule or policy covers.

CreationSubjectKind.description: What a creation rule's subject names.

reason.description: Shown to administrators; not to the account holder.

ErrorBody.description: Body of every non-2xx response; `code` is stable and machine-readable.

ExternalIdentityInfo.description: A provider identity linked to an account.

email.description: The address the provider last gave, if it vouched for one.

name.description: What to call it on the sign-in button.

sign_in_url.description: Send the browser here (a full page navigation, with an optional `return_to` path) to start signing in.

data.description: Base64 of the commit's body, as in a push.

pointers.description: The revisions the commit's pointer cache records: what it wrote and what a merge adopted, ordered by path.

trees.description: The trees the commit adds against its first parent, as in a push.

head.description: The branch's head when the fetch started; null for a branch with no commit.

branches.description: The branches to fetch; every branch if empty. Ignored when `cursor` is given.

haves.description: Commits the client already has, normally its branch heads; ids the repository does not know are ignored.

limit.description: Commits per page; the server's default and cap apply when omitted or larger.

next.description: Opaque; send it as `cursor` for the next page. Absent on the last page.

file_mode.description: The head revision's git file mode; `100644` when there is no revision.

revision.description: Head revision; absent if the path is locked but has no revision yet.

FileMode.description: Git's file mode for a file: regular, executable or symbolic link (whose content is the link target).

next_after.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page; null on the last page.

reason.description: Why the lock is being removed; required and recorded in the audit log.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `before` to fetch the next, older page; null on the last page and with `path`.

revisions.description: With `path`: all of that path's revisions, oldest first. Without: newest first.

Limits.description: Limits on one owner. Every limit is opt-in: a null field is unlimited.

members.description: Members an organization may have; always null for a user.

storage_bytes.description: Bytes of distinct content across the owner's repositories.

LimitsListing.description: The server default and every owner that has limits of its own.

defaults.description: Applies to owners with nothing of their own; all null unless the operator configures it.

Me.description: The caller and what they may do in one repository.

role.description: The effective role: the highest of the direct grant, team grants and organization ownership.

MemberCreation.description: What members may create when no rule applies.

MemberSource.description: What decides a member's effective role.

MergeChange.description: A path the merge changes in the target, with the content it ends up with.

content.description: The git blob id of the merged content.

oneOf.description: The versions to merge line by line, present only when no revision holds the result.

revision.description: A revision of the path that holds exactly this content and file mode, when one does.

oneOf.description: For `exclusive_conversion`: what happened to the path and when, when the history shows it.

MergeConversion.description: The conversion of a path to exclusive that a merge conflict met, and the shared version it stranded.

diverged_revision.description: The diverged shared revision the conversion stranded, with its author and time.

policy_revision.description: The policy revision in force at the conversion.

revision.description: The conversion revision, the first of the path's exclusive line.

MergeFastForward.description: Whether a merge may or must fast-forward.

MergeInputs.description: The versions a path's merge is made from; a side is null where the path does not exist.

base_inline.description: The base's bytes, base64, when no revision holds it (a virtual base), so a client can still merge against it.

MergeReport.description: What a merge does, or did.

bases.description: The merge base commits; more than one means a criss-cross history.

changes.description: Paths whose content changes in the target, ordered by path.

commit.description: The commit the merge wrote; null for a preview and for an up-to-date merge.

stranded.description:
Shared versions on other branches that the policy file a merge into the default branch brought stranded;
empty for a preview and for every other merge.

target_commit.description: The target's head the merge was computed on; null for a branch with no commits.

virtual_base.description: True when the bases were merged into a virtual one.

MergeRequest.description: A source (a branch, or a commit) merged into a target branch.

expect_target.description: The commit the caller saw as the target's head; if the branch has moved the answer is `merge_stale`.

message.description: The merge commit's message; `Merge branch '<source>' into <target>` if omitted.

resolutions.description: The content chosen for each conflicted path (and optionally for a path that merged cleanly).

source.description: A branch name, or a commit id or abbreviation of at least 4 digits.

target.description: The branch that moves; the default branch if omitted.

MergeResolution.description: The content chosen for one path of a merge: an uploaded object, by its blob id.

oneOf.description: Git's file mode of the content; regular if omitted.

MergeSide.description: One version of a path in a merge.

content.description: The git blob id of the content.

revision.description: The revision that holds this version; null for the virtual base of a criss-cross merge.

MissingObjectsRequest.description: Chunk digests to check against the server's object store.

hashes.description: SHA-256 hex of each chunk's bytes; at most 10000.

missing.description: The digests from the request that the server does not store.

MyLock.description: A live lock the caller holds, with the repository it is in.

OidcLink.description: Where to send the browser to link the provider to the signed-in account.

OrgInfo.description: An organization: a namespace that owns repositories.

oneOf.description: The caller's standing in it (`owner` or `member`); absent when they have none.

OrgRole.description: A person's standing in an organization.

OwnerKind.description: What an owner (a user or an organization) is.

OwnerLimits.description: An owner's limits. Nothing is limited unless an operator sets a limit or a server default.

effective.description: The limits in force: the owner's own where set, else the server default, else null (unlimited).

own.description: Limits set for this owner alone; a null field follows the server default.

OwnerUsage.description: What an owner uses against its limits.

Person.description: A commit's author or committer, apart from the time (the commit's `created_at`).

PolicyPreview.description: What a proposed policy would change in the repository, without applying it.

released_locks.description: Live locks that would be released because their path becomes shared.

stranded.description: Diverged shared versions on other branches of the paths that would become exclusive; each would be stranded.

to_exclusive.description: Paths that are shared now and would become exclusive.

to_shared.description: Paths that are exclusive now and would become shared.

PushObject.description: One git object of a push: its id and its body (the bytes after git's `<kind> <length>` header), base64.

id.description: The object id the body hashes to under the repository's algorithm (SHA-256).

branch.description: The branch to append to; the default branch if omitted.

commits.description: The commits, oldest first; the first is a child of the branch's head, each next one of the one before.

trees.description: The trees the commits need that the server may not have. Blobs are uploaded beforehand through the object routes.

head.description: The branch's head commit after the push.

revisions.description: The revisions the commits made, in commit order, each commit's by path.

stranded.description: Shared versions on other branches that a policy file in the push stranded; omitted when there are none.

content.description: The object's git blob id; for a chunk upload, the SHA-256 hex of its bytes.

email.description: Required when the server is open and verifies email addresses (`RegistrationInfo.email_verification`).

invite.description: Required when the server is invite only.

status.description:
`active`, or what the account still needs: `pending_verification` (follow the link in the email) or
`pending_approval` (an administrator must approve it).

approval.description: With `open` registration: an administrator approves each new account after it is verified.

email_verification.description:
With `open` registration: sign-up needs an email address, and the account stays inactive until its
link is followed.

lease_hours.description: How long a lock lasts before it expires unless renewed.

max_locks_per_user.description:
Locks one user may hold in the repository: the policy file's `meta.max_locks_per_user` if it sets one, else
the repository setting, else the server default.

max_locks_per_user_setting.description: The repository setting alone; absent when it follows the server default. Not in force while the policy file sets one.

max_locks_set_by_policy.description: True when `.pyn/pyn.toml` sets the limit; the setting then cannot be changed.

role.description: The caller's role in the repository; absent when they have none.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page; null on the last page.

RepoPolicyInfo.description: An organization's repository-creation policy. Owners can always create repositories and are not listed in it.

member_creation.description: What members may create when no rule applies; `none` (owners only) is the default.

rules.description: Ordered by kind, subject, then effect.

files.description: Paths with at least one revision on the default branch.

locks.description: Live locks with their holders, ordered by path.

updated_at.description: Time of the newest revision; absent for an empty repository.

RepoTeam.description: A team of the owning organization and its role in a repository.

base_revision.description: The current head the caller is looking at; must still be the head.

branch.description: The branch the restore is committed on; the default branch if omitted.

confirm.description: `<path>@r<base_revision>`, confirming the caller knows which head is being replaced.

revision.description: The older revision whose content becomes the new head.

oneOf.description: The structured author the v2 hash covers; absent for a v1 revision, whose hash predates it.

base.description:
The revision this one was based on, the committing branch's revision of the path; absent when the branch had
none. Not covered by `hash`; `pyn verify` checks that it names an older revision of the path.

changeset.description: Shared by the revisions checked in together as one changeset; absent for a single-path checkin.

commit.description: The id of the commit this revision belongs to; see `Commit`.

content.description: The content's git blob id (SHA-256 hex of `blob <len>\0` followed by the content).

deleted.description:
The revision removes the path from its branch; `content` and `file_mode` are those of the version removed.
Its `hash_version` is 3.

file_mode.description: The git file mode of the content.

hash.description: SHA-256 hex over the revision's canonical encoding, by `hash_version` (docs/concepts/integrity.md).

hash_version.description: The encoding `hash` uses: 1 or 2. Version 2 requires `author_identity`, version 1 forbids it.

legacy_content.description:
The content string this revision's `hash` covers, when it differs from `content`: revisions that predate blob
ids, whose hash covers the SHA-256 hex of the bare content.

oneOf.description: The path's mode when the revision was made; absent for revisions that predate recording it.

previous.description: The hash of the path's previous revision by number; absent for the first.

restored_from.description: Set when this revision restored the content of an earlier one.

stranded.description:
Only in the response to checking in or restoring `.pyn/pyn.toml` on the default branch: the diverged shared
versions on other branches that the change stranded. Empty, and omitted, everywhere else.

created_by.description: The server administrator who created it.

csrf_token.description: Send as the `X-Pyn-CSRF` header on every POST, PUT and DELETE.

SetLimitsRequest.description: Fields left out stay as they are; a number sets the limit and `null` returns the field to the server default.

members.description: Organizations only; a user has no member limit.

user.description: The first administrator, who can now sign in with the password.

public_url.description: The address people reach the web app at; verification links use it.

token.description: The one-time setup token from the server's log or its `PYN_SETUP_TOKEN` setting.

SetupStatus.description: Whether first-run setup has happened; carries no secrets.

public_url.description: What setup recorded; before setup, the address the server is configured with.

registration.description: What setup recorded, or the configured default before setup.

server_name.description: Set once setup recorded a name.

SignInOptions.description: How people can sign in to this server.

oneOf.description: The configured external provider; null when the server has none.

password.description: Whether anyone may sign in with a password. When false, server administrators still can.

SnapshotEntry.description: A path as of a commit: the revision the commit's ancestry gives it. `mode` is what `.pyn/pyn.toml` says at that commit.

content.description: The content's git blob id at that revision.

SnapshotPage.description: The whole repository as of one commit.

commit.description: The id of the commit the entries are as of; null for a repository with no commits.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page; null on the last page.

StrandedVersion.description:
A shared version a branch holds of a path that became exclusive on the default branch (decision #38). It stays in
history but can no longer merge into the path's single line.

branch.description: The branch that holds the version.

branch_owner.description: Who created the branch; the audit log tells them (`version_stranded`).

commit.description: The commit the revision belongs to.

conversion.description: The conversion revision the default branch made when the path became exclusive; absent in a preview.

revision.description: The stranded revision of the path.

TeamInfo.description: A team of an organization with its members and repository roles.

TeamRepo.description: A repository where a team holds a role.

repos.description: `owner/name` of each repository the token is limited to; empty means every repository.

oneOf.description: The newest revision at or under the entry (`path` on it names the file). Absent for a file with a lock but no revision.
The live lock on a file; always absent for folders.

path.description: Repo-relative path; pass it as `path` to list a folder.

entries.description: Folders first, then files, each by name.

path.description: The listed folder; empty for the root.

UpdateRepoRequest.description: Fields left out stay as they are.

max_locks_per_user.description: A number sets the limit, `null` returns to the server default. Refused while the policy file sets one.

oneOf.description: Changing it needs the owner with admin rights and is recorded in the audit log.

UpdateTeamRequest.description: Fields left out stay as they are.

members.description: Organization members; null for a user.

stored_bytes.description: Bytes of distinct content, counted once per repository.

token.description: The token from the verification link.

VerifyProblem.description:
One break found by verification: `hash_mismatch` (a record's fields do not give its hash), `version_mismatch` (a revision's `hash_version` disagrees with its stored fields), `broken_link` (it does
not follow the record before it) or `base_mismatch` (a revision's base is not an older revision of its path). Revision breaks carry `path` and `revision`; audit breaks carry `event`.

commit.description: The commit id, for a problem in a commit record.

audit_events.description: Events checked; null when the audit log was not checked (a single path, or no `view_audit`).

Visibility.description: Public: anyone, signed in or not, may read the repository. Private: members only, and everyone else gets 404.
